title: Wgpu Renderer Full Parity
description: Bring the wgpu renderer (framework/renderer/wgpu, ui/wgpu, infinite/world) to full visual and functional parity with the React reference renderer (framework/renderer/react). Scope: restore compile after ViewState locale/terminology schema change; close the five open wgpu tickets (window options chip z-order, render plan validator, lowpoly dev boot, world3d empty preview, 3d component hover/select/edge-preview); implement the three placeholder-only componentScene surfaces (puzzle2d-board, icon-render, note-canvas); shell parity sweep (presence overlay, dead code cleanup); extend the wgpu playground e2e harness to compare against React reference screenshots and produce a parity report across all ~30 playgrounds.
summary:
Implemented the `puzzle2d-board` componentScene surface in the wgpu-native renderer, closing the last of the three placeholder-only surfaces in scope for this ticket (icon-render and note-canvas were completed by concurrent sessions on the same shared ticket during this work).

Added `puzzle_2d = { path = "../../../../puzzle/2d/rs" }` to the wgpu crate's Cargo.toml and used `puzzle_2d::BoardHost` directly as a plain Rust type (no wasm-bindgen wrapper), mirroring the existing `gis_2d::MapHost` integration pattern in `engine_canvas`:

- `EngineSurface` gained `board_host: Option<BoardHost>`, `board_sync_cache: BoardSyncCache`, `board_pending_events: Vec<BoardEventRow>`, and `board_pointer_inside: bool`.
- `sync_board_host` diffs each `Puzzle2dBoardScene` field against a cache and applies only changes onto the host — reparsing the fixture triggers a silent re-application of selection/camera immediately after (since `parse_fixture_v1` resets both), and all fixture/selection/camera sync is skipped while `host.defers_descriptor_sync_from_js()` is true (mid-gesture), matching the React host's `pendingFixtureSceneRef` deferred-apply behavior without needing its explicit timer, since the per-frame cache-diff naturally avoids re-fighting a locally-mutated camera/selection.
- `paint_puzzle_board` builds the frame via `host.build_vector_scene()` (an `infinite_cavas::Scene`, same type gis_2d returns) composited through the existing `render_vello_scene` vello-offscreen-texture pipeline.
- Ported `coalescePuzzle2dBoardEvents` from the React host verbatim as `coalesce_puzzle2d_board_events` (drops transient rows, coalesces `camera` to latest and `nodeMove` to one row per id unless `nodeDragEnd` follows, flags flush-now events) — 6 unit tests added in a new `puzzle2d_board_engine_tests` module, all passing.
- Ported `buildPuzzle2dSelectionMenuItems` as `build_puzzle2d_selection_menu_items` in the `scenes` module (Hide/Show, Lock/Unlock, Duplicate, Select-same-kind, Zoom-to-selection, Delete, or "Select all" when nothing is selected).
- Pointer/wheel primitives (`puzzle_board_pointer_down/move/up/leave`, `puzzle_board_wheel`) forward raw screen coordinates into `BoardHost`'s own interaction state machine (it handles select-rect/lasso, node drag, and brush internally — no external `SceneDragMode` bookkeeping needed, unlike gis2d-map's marquee), then drain+coalesce+dispatch `applyBoardEvents`/`setCamera` commands exactly matching the React host's buffering semantics (`drainAndMaybeFlush` on move, unconditional `flushBoardEvents` on up/leave/wheel).
- Added `Puzzle2dBoardSurface` (bounds, controller_id, fixture_json) threaded through `render_ui_node`/`render_ui_node_inner`/`render_component_scene`, `ShellState` (field, `new()` init, per-frame `.clear()`), and the two `render_ui_node` call sites — mirroring `GisMapSurface`'s plumbing exactly, alongside the concurrently-added `icon_render_states`.
- Wired `AppRuntime::handle_pointer_button` (both down and up branches), `handle_pointer_move`, and the `frame()` wheel-dispatch block with puzzle2d-board loops mirroring the gis2d-map loops precisely, including a `board_drag_active` check (via `defers_descriptor_sync_from_js() || is_dragging_area_select()`) so pointer-up outside the surface bounds still reaches the host mid-gesture.
- Right-click context menu: `open_puzzle2d_board_context_menu` picks the most-specific target via `BoardHost::pick_targets_at_screen_json` + max-generality selection, eagerly replaces the selection (silently on the host, plus a real `setSelection` dispatch) if the clicked target wasn't already selected, then pushes `build_puzzle2d_selection_menu_items`' output as `ContextMenuItem`s — matching the React host's `onContextMenu` eager-select behavior, wired into `ShellState::handle_pointer_button`'s existing button==2 branch alongside gis2d-map's.
- Added a `puzzle2d-wgpu-dev` launch.json entry (port 6112, `SEMIO_PLUGIN=puzzle`, `SEMIO_RENDERER=wgpu`) — note the registered wasm plugin id is `puzzle` (a single crate covering 2d/3d/5d), not `puzzle2d`; `SEMIO_PLUGIN=puzzle2d` produces "no wasm plugin modules found for filter puzzle2d" at boot.

Deliberately out of scope: keyboard shortcuts (Escape cancel-area-select, Tab brush-cycle, Cmd/Ctrl+A select-all, Delete) and an explicit DOM-style pointer-leave concept beyond bounds-exit detection — the task's core ask was pointer/wheel/context-menu, and there's no native "left the canvas" event in this single-window immediate-mode renderer to hang a truer leave semantic on.

Verified: `cargo check -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu` compiles cleanly (only pre-existing warnings, none from this change). `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --manifest-path framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/Cargo.toml` (via `trunk build`) also compiles cleanly. `cargo test -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu --lib puzzle2d`: 6/6 passing.

Not verified: live interactive visual comparison against `SEMIO_RENDERER=react` in the browser. The wasm build repeatedly succeeded at the `cargo build` step but then failed at trunk's asset-pipeline stage ("error writing JS loader file to stage dir: No such file or directory") — a stage-directory collision between concurrent `trunk serve` processes from other chat sessions sharing this machine's filesystem, reproduced identically across three separate rebuild attempts over ~50 minutes of waiting. This is an environment/infrastructure limitation, not a defect surfaced by this code. The `puzzle2d-wgpu-dev` launch config is in place and ready for a follow-up visual check once a preview slot and a non-colliding build window are available. Separately flagged and out of scope: `cargo test -p puzzle_2d --lib` fails to compile due to a pre-existing broken `include_str!("../fixture/...")` path unrelated to this change (spawned as a separate background task suggestion).
